title: Experiment: `@mdx-js/mdx` infers plain markdown from a `.md` path, and the contract goes silent
summary:
Compiling `# Doc\n\nMARKER` through the restricted plugin with `path: "x.md"` and no `format` option produced `

Doc

MARKER

` — the mapped component rendered as a bare paragraph. Compiling `Inline {1 + 1} expression.` the same way COMPILED SUCCESSFULLY with no rejection. With `format: "mdx"` passed explicitly, the same two inputs produced the mapped component's `
` and a refusal naming the file and line:column respectively.

omissions.reason: Only `.md` and an explicit `format` were exercised. Whether a pathless or unusual extension behaves as a third case was not tested; the fix removes the dependency on the path entirely.

notes: ⚠️ THE DANGEROUS HALF IS THE SECOND ONE. A component quietly rendering as a paragraph is visible to anyone looking at the page. An EXPRESSION COMPILING WITH NO REJECTION is not visible to anyone: the plugin runs, finds no expression nodes because the parser never produced any, and reports success. The entire restricted-MDX contract becomes vacuous, silently, decided by a filename. ⚠️ IT HAD ALREADY MADE A TEST LIE. The suite's 'every REAL stage document compiles under the restricted contract' case passed on all nine documents before the format was pinned — not because they are contract-clean, but because they are `.md` and were never subjected to the rules. They do pass with `format: "mdx"`, which is why the finding cost nothing beyond the measurement.
